forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Maidstone's long-term borrowing rose from £62.4m to £83.3m in 2025/26, its accounts show
news_drafts.lead:
Maidstone Borough Council's long-term borrowing rose by £20.95m, or 33.5%, from £62.366m at 31 March 2025 to £83.317m at 31 March 2026. The figures are in its statement of accounts for 2025/26 (the council's formal annual accounts), which went to the Audit, Governance and Standards Committee on 28 September.

The council's external auditor (an independent check on its accounts) reported that temporary accommodation and homelessness services overspent by £0.586m against a budget of £4.295m, or 13.6%. The auditor described "significant demand and cost pressures" and said demand remains volatile and hard to predict. Mitigating actions were in place, but the council reached an overall balanced position only because higher treasury and investment income, meaning earnings from its cash and investments, offset the overspend.

A separate budget risk paper looks at the possible reorganisation of Kent's councils. It says Kent County Council and Medway Council together account for 87% of the net day-to-day spending of the 14 existing authorities, and both already face significant budget gaps. Medway was granted exceptional financial support in 2025/26, which is government permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending. The paper says projected savings may not be achievable and that borrowing before a new council takes over "could have major implications for the cash flow of a new unitary, including headroom for further borrowing."

findings.paper_title: Agreement to Lease Commercial Space -Maidstone East
findings.headline: The council states the financial returns meet its current hurdle rates
findings.detail: The finance section says the financial returns meet the council's current hurdle rates, together with the proposed third-party funding, and that the arrangement will produce a rate of return on capital already in the programme. The paper gives no rate or return figure in the body.
findings.matters: A hurdle-rate claim without a published return figure is a point a finance director would test against the exempt financial model, and peers would look at how the claim is supported.
findings.quote: The financial returns meet the councils current hurdle rates

findings.paper_title: Agreement to Lease Commercial Space -Maidstone East
findings.headline: The funding package includes CIL and S106 contributions alongside NHS capital, with amounts in Exempt Appendix 1
findings.detail: Paragraph 2.15 lists the funding components to be secured through the MoU and Section 2 agreement, including a base level of NHS capital, design fees, NHS-funded capital package, a CIL contribution from the earlier Round 2 allocations, and an S106 contribution. The total package is in Exempt Appendix 1 (Fig G).
findings.matters: Stacking CIL and S106 money with NHS capital is a funding structure other councils with regeneration schemes can compare, and it shows how the council's own capital requirement is being reduced.
findings.figures: Total package up to Fig. G in Exempt Appendix 1; individual components at Figs A to F, none stated in the body
findings.quote: A contribution of S106 monies as per Fig. F.

findings.paper_title: Agreement to Lease Commercial Space -Maidstone East
findings.headline: Design fees for the NHS business case are to be indemnified by the NHS under a Memorandum of Understanding, with architect work due by 31/10/2026
findings.detail: The council intends to appoint an architect from the NHS Shared Business Services Framework for RIBA stage 3 design, with fees capped at Fig. B in Exempt Appendix 1. Any RIBA stage 4 fees, capped at Fig. C, are to be indemnified by the NHS under a Memorandum of Understanding. The stage 3 work is due by 31/10/2026.
findings.matters: The council is paying design fees ahead of the NHS business case approval, and the indemnity is the mechanism that protects it from those costs if the NHS does not proceed.
findings.figures: Stage 3 fee cap at Fig. B and stage 4 fee cap at Fig. C in Exempt Appendix 1 (not stated in body); completion date 31/10/2026
findings.quote: MBC will be indemnified for all fees by the NHS with the relevant Memorandum of Understanding in place to secure this.

findings.paper_title: Agreement to Lease Commercial Space -Maidstone East
findings.headline: The NHS funding arrangement is at the stage of Section 2 Heads of Terms, with the Section 2 contract still to be agreed
findings.detail: The programme section lists the NHS Strategic Outline Case as receiving initial support in January 2026, a Memorandum of Understanding agreed in principle in summer 2026, and Section 2 Heads of Terms issued by the NHS in September 2026. The NHS business case still has to be approved.
findings.matters: Council expenditure is being committed ahead of the signed funding contract, so a reader can see that the stated third-party funding is not yet legally in place.
findings.figures: Strategic Outline Case initial support January 2026; Heads of Terms September 2026
findings.quote: Section 2 Heads of Terms issued by NHS in September 2026

findings.paper_title: Agreement to Lease Commercial Space -Maidstone East
findings.headline: Maidstone Borough Council will lease the Maidstone East commercial space to the NHS at a peppercorn rent, with no rental income payable to the council
findings.detail: The report recommends granting the lease at a peppercorn rent, with the council receiving no rental income from the commercial space. The paper says the council could otherwise seek full market rent, and that the arrangement should be considered in the round against the reduced capital requirement.
findings.matters: A finance director, here or elsewhere, can see that a commercial asset is being let at no rent in exchange for third-party-funded fit-out and a reduced capital requirement, which changes the income profile of a regeneration scheme.
findings.figures: Commercial accommodation of approximately 1,863m² (20,000 sq ft); peppercorn rent; no rental income
findings.quote: The lease would be granted at a peppercorn rent, with no rental income payable to the Council.
